segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped
or, in the event of a yield sign,
slowed
or stopped,
the driver
shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection
from such through highway
or which are approaching
so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: Traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) controlled by a police officer: dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ... police_officer' governing x's approach carrier or i (dev.governs); x is a member of the traffic controlled.
A dev.traffic_signal governing x's approach carrier or i (dev.governs), not dev.inoperative and not dark: traffic 'alternately directed to stop or proceed' (DEF-NRS-484A-290).

dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' or dev.yield_sign 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt' governing (dev.governs) the carrier x approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) or i; status read from presence.
Vehicle aggregate; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Having stopped: a halt (drv.motion.stopped, 'complete cessation from movement') at an observation at which x occupies its approach carrier c (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c i) with its footprint outside i, since x last came onto c and before its current occupancy of i began - the words name a stop and no place, so the halt is read wherever on the approach it was made.
In the event of a yield sign: a dev.yield_sign governs c or i (dev.governs) and no stop sign does.
Or stopped: the halt of s6 (drv.motion.stopped) also meets the yield-sign alternative.
The same driver, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is not moving into or within the intersection (drv.motion.moving with rel.occupies of st.intersection) into a predicted conflict with a vehicle owed precedence.
Other vehicles y (aggregate) which have entered i: y's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and has since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i.
From such through highway: cy lies on (st.on_way) a st.highway that i lies on and x's approach carrier c does not, the through highway the sibling node's place reads.
Approaching: y occupies a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i ('a road user occupying one such carrier approaches through it'), outside i.
During the time the driver is moving across or within the intersection: x is moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint overlapping i (rel.occupies, st.intersection), its entry included.

operationalizations.standard: slowed (in the event of a yield sign)
operationalizations.convention: A vehicle at a yield-controlled approach has slowed where its speed (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity') fell to or below the yield-control check speed of the intersection-sight-distance model at some observation on its approach carrier outside the intersection since it last came onto it.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance: a vehicle approaching on the through highway (its carrier on the through way, st.on_way, st.highway) is an immediate hazard during the subject's crossing where its time to reach the intersection is at most the critical gap: its ground distance to i (st.region_geometry) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps an intersection i and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where x's approach carrier c (the carrier with st.lane_enters c i x occupied when its current occupancy of i began) or i is governed by a stop sign or a yield sign (dev.governs), and, at the entry of the current occupancy, no police officer's direction (dev.human_direction role police_officer) and no traffic signal that is neither inoperative nor dark governed c or i; where x, at some observation since it last came onto c and before that entry, with its footprint on c outside i, was halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance), or - where only a yield sign governs - had a speed (kin.speed) at or below p.yield_sign_check_speed; and where there is a vehicle y other than x such that (a) y's footprint overlaps i and has since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i lying on (st.on_way) a highway that i lies on and c does not, or (b) y occupies such a carrier cy outside i and its ground distance to i (st.region_geometry) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: No vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'Proper signs ... erected' is read from the presence of a stop or yield sign governing the approach.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'.
rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' on st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; the entry is the observation at which the overlap last became true.

dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered'; dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', the intersection or a carrier entering it (st.lane_enters).
dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation through a past operator, the moment the words fix.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; the class is the vehicle aggregate.

'Such a stop' is the stop the sibling words require, with every qualification they keep: a halt (drv.motion.stopped, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') made on x's approach carrier c (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c i, st.travel_region) before this entry and since the approach began, at the governing place - the st.stop_line marking c (st.entrance_of), else the st.crosswalk marking c with the footprint not overlapping it, else c's entrance end outside st.intersection where st.sight_along_way along a through st.highway (st.on_way) meets the view bound - within the stop-point tolerance of it (st.region_geometry) on its upstream side (prim.region_offset_along along c's direction).
The same driver, read through the vehicle's controlled motion; vehicle aggregate.
Proceeding is the subject's motion (drv.motion.moving, speed above the resolution) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection), the entry included.

The vehicles yielded to (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle): a vehicle y that previously completed a stop halted (drv.motion.stopped, 'complete cessation from movement') on its own approach carrier cy whose entrance end is i (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), outside i, its halt beginning before x's halt on c (time since y's halt rose greater than time since x's); or a vehicle y whose footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: cautiously (proceeding, yielding)
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds cautiously, yielding, where it moves without creating a conflict with a vehicle it must yield to - no such vehicle whose centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the time-to-collision horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where: at the entry of the current occupancy (the observation at which x's overlap with i last became true) at least one installed, uncovered traffic signal head governed i or a carrier entering i and every such head governing i or x's approach carrier was inoperative (read at that entry observation through a past operator); and x made such a stop before that entry: on its approach carrier c (the carrier with st.lane_enters c i x occupied at the observation before the entry), since its approach to the governing place began, x was halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) at that place as NRS_484B_250_4_o1 reads it - the stop line marking c, else before the crosswalk marking c, else outside i at c's entrance end where st.sight_along_way along a through highway is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance - within p.stop_point_tolerance of it on its upstream side; and there is a vehicle y other than x such that (a) y's footprint overlaps i, or (b) y occupies a carrier cy whose entrance end is i, outside i, and halted on cy (drv.motion.stopped) since it last came onto cy, its halt beginning earlier than x's halt on c.
obligation: No vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach, under constant velocities, within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Cautiously' is read only through the yield the words attach to it: the subject does not move within the intersection into a predicted conflict with a vehicle it must yield to; no further speed or manner bound is read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Intersection i's only signal head is uncovered and dev.inoperative. x halts at the stop line of its approach lane c, then moves into i at 4 m/s while vehicle y, within i on the crossing way, crosses x's path; prim.closest_approach_distance is 1 m at 1.2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x moves into i only while y, still within i, is leaving on the far side: predicted closest approach 9 m.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing i shows circular_green (not inoperative) when x enters; x moves through i next to y.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but dev.inoperative is not observed, so the condition at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: y halted on its approach cy before x halted at its stop line; as x moves into i, y starts into i and their predicted closest approach is 0.8 m within 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x halts at its stop line, then moves through i with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x never halted on c before entering (kin.speed stays above the tolerance): the condition 'after making such a stop' does not hold.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
param_proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

param_proposals.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal of intention is the signal itself, never a declared intention (the ontology: 'a signal "of intention" is the signal'): sig.turn_indicator ('state ∈ {off, left, right}') or sig.hand_signal ('a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, ...}'), of the side of the turn; not a stand-in for the turn itself, which is judged separately through motion. Turning right or left, or otherwise from a direct course, is the heading departing to that side from the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies: drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction, the signed departure (left positive) of kin.heading from st.lane_direction, on a carrier of kind st.travel_region x occupies (rel.occupies). 'continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a window in distance travelled (a .path window), which reads kin.path_length ('distance travelled along the body's path'); the figure is the law's literal.
'not less than the last 300 feet traveled' is the same .path window over kin.path_length with the law's other literal, the bound selected outside a business or residence district.

Changing the course is the event at which the heading's departure from the occupied carrier's direction (drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction over kin.heading and st.lane_direction, on a st.travel_region x occupies) first exceeds the course-change tolerance to a side: the observation at which that condition became true. The signal window lies behind it ('prior to').
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway').

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.

residues.why: The words say the rule holds in every weather; no weather condition restricts or extends the duty, which is the same whether or not it rains, snows or is clear.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that changes course at the judged observation: x occupies a travel region c with a designated direction, and drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction(x, c) rises above p.course_change_sin_tolerance (a change to the left) or below its negative (a change to the right) at this observation, not having done so at the observation before (rises).
obligation: At that observation, a signal of the side of the change held at every observation of the window of path length x travelled behind it (holdsFor .path): for a change to the left, sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left; for a change to the right, state right or meaning right. The window's length is selected with Term.cond: the literal 100 ft where asm.business_or_residence_district holds, the literal 300 ft where it does not. A window reaching before the start of the trace leaves the verdict unknown.

narrowings.why: Turning right or left and otherwise turning from a direct course are read as the heading departing from the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies; a change of course made where the vehicle occupies no carrier with a designated direction is not judged.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle in a lane with a designated direction, asm.business_or_residence_district declared true, lights sig.turn_indicator left only over the last 10 m of path before its heading departs to the left of the lane direction beyond the tolerance; the trace covers more than 100 ft behind the change.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle and district, with sig.turn_indicator left lit at every observation of the last 50 m of path before the heading departs to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle drives along its lane with its heading aligned with the lane direction throughout; no change of course occurs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle changes course to the left in its lane in a district; the source observes neither turn indicators nor arm signals.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district declared false; the vehicle signals right over the last 50 m of path (above 100 ft but below 300 ft) before its heading departs to the right of the lane direction.

param_proposals.name: p.course_change_sin_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Lane-change kinematics: the heading of a vehicle changing lanes or turning departs from the lane direction by about three degrees or more, a smaller departure being in-lane steering correction; the bound is the sine of that angle.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic lane-change trajectory studies (heading-angle distributions of lane changes, e.g. Toledo and Zohar 2007; NGSIM lane-change analyses).

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and: The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle'; 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The intersection is the region the intention is declared at and the vehicle enters: a st.intersection, anchored by the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters).

The highway has a right turn lane 'as set forth in subsection 4', whose words are 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning': a st.turn_lane of side right that is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency, ordinal equal to count) on (st.on_way) the highway (st.highway) of the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies), entering the intersection x enters (st.lane_enters, st.intersection). This node applies where the highway has none (the 'or' of the words).

The extreme right lane is the st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency: 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'); the turn is made from it when, at the observation before the entry, the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters, st.intersection) is that lane. Not a stand-in for a lateral offset: lane membership is the lane x occupies, not its distance to the edge.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.
The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the qualifiers 'single', 'right lane' and 'to be used only for turning', which set forth what the highway's right turn lane is; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (driving in that lane only to turn right) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the same qualifiers from the same opening words of subsection 4; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (not travelling through an intersection from that lane) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that enters an intersection i at the judged observation (rel.occupies(x, i) rises), with int.turn_right(x, i) declared true at that observation; and the highway has no right turn lane: at the observation before the entry no st.turn_lane of side right that enters i, lies on the highway of a carrier x occupies entering i, and is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency ordinal equal to count) exists.
obligation: At the observation before the entry, x occupies a st.lane l with st.lane_enters(l, i) whose st.lane_adjacency ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction, and every lane x occupies there that enters i is such a lane. Violated where x enters i with its intention to turn right from a lane entering i that is not the extreme right lane.

narrowings.why: The turn is judged at the observation before the entry, by the lane through which x approaches the intersection then; an approach on a roadway without marked lanes, where no lane ordinal exists, leaves the extreme right lane unknown.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-lane approach without a right turn lane, a car with int.turn_right declared at the intersection enters it from the lane of ordinal 1 of 2.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car enters the intersection from the lane of ordinal 2 of 2.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The approach has a right turn lane entering the intersection; the extreme-right-lane requirement does not apply.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car with int.turn_right enters from one of two lanes; the source does not supply lane ordinals.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.

After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: Traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') being controlled by a police officer: dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ... police_officer' governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier of x or the intersection i. The traffic controlled is the traffic on x's approach, x itself a member of it.

Traffic being controlled by a traffic-control signal (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'): a dev.traffic_signal head governing x's approach carrier or i (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication') and not in state dark; an inoperative head directs nothing.

Proper signs are dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' or dev.yield_sign 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt' governing (dev.governs) the carrier x approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) or the intersection; propriety and erection by authority are read from the sign's presence.
Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' when required is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.stopped); 'yield' at the place, under a yield sign, is what the next sentence names, 'slowed or stopped': a halt or a speed (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity') at or below the yield-control check speed. The place, in order: st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device' recorded as marking x's carrier (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); else st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' marking it, with the footprint not yet overlapping it (rel.occupies); else the carrier's entrance end at st.intersection, with the footprint outside it. At the place is within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry body distance), upstream along the carrier's direction (prim.region_offset_along), on the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters, st.travel_region).

operationalizations.standard: has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway
operationalizations.convention: The view of approaching traffic on the through highway is a sight distance along that way (st.sight_along_way 'within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye') at least the stopping sight distance of the approach-speed design convention. The through highway is a st.highway the intersection lies on (st.on_way) and x's approach carrier does not: the way whose traffic the sign on x's approach makes x yield to (DEF-NRS-484A-275 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield').

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into an intersection i (x's footprint overlaps i and did not at the observation before), where at the observation before the entry x occupied a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters c i, and a stop sign or yield sign governs c or i (dev.governs). Not applicable where, at the entry observation, x's traffic is controlled by a police officer (a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs c or i) or by a traffic signal (a dev.traffic_signal governing c or i that is not dev.inoperative and not in state dark).
obligation: Event: the entry of x into i. Approach: the carrier c x occupies at the observation before the entry with st.lane_enters c i; where several such carriers give different verdicts, unknown. Act: where a stop sign governs c or i, a halt (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign governs, a halt or a speed (kin.speed) at or below p.yield_sign_check_speed. Place, in the words' order: (1) a stop line s recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c); (2) where c's stop-line association is observed and lists none, a crosswalk w recorded as marking c, the act made with x's footprint not overlapping w; (3) where neither is recorded (associations observed), the entrance end of c: with x's footprint outside i within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, at an observation at which st.sight_along_way from x to the through highway h (a st.highway i lies on and c does not, st.on_way) is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance. The act counts at an observation at which x is on c, outside i, on the upstream side of the place (prim.region_offset_along along c's designated direction, the place itself included) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance between x's body and the place). History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the place marks, is short of the place and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) or at x's previous entry into i through the same place. Met where the act is found; violated where the search reaches either end without it; unknown only where it reaches neither (the recording begins inside the stopping zone with no act recorded), and unknown where the carrier association, its direction or the sight distance is unobserved and the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: 'Proper signs ... erected' is read from the presence of a stop or yield sign governing the approach.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'Clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents.

'Yield' at the place under a yield sign is read, by the words of the next sentence, as slowing to at most the yield-control check speed or halting there; 'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view' is read as the entrance end of the approach carrier at which the view bound is met.
The driver's view is read as what could be seen from the place along the through way (st.sight_along_way), not as what the driver perceived.
The through highway's designation is read from the stop or yield sign governing the subject's approach: every way the intersection lies on that the approach carrier does not.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs lane c (st.lane_enters c i); stop line s marks c. No signal or officer controls c or i. x approaches from 80 m at 12 m/s, slows to 2 m/s at s and enters i without kin.speed reaching the tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same; x halts 0.3 m short of s, then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or i; x enters without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but dev.governs is not observed, so whether the stop sign governs x's approach is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Only a dev.yield_sign governs c; x slows to 3 m/s within 1 m short of s without halting, then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs i and directs x to proceed.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with x already within the stopping zone of s on c, creeping at 0.8 m/s; no halt is recorded and x enters i.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start of x on c (its last observation outside the stopping zone of s), before the recording begins

param_proposals.convention: Speed to which a vehicle at a yield-controlled approach slows so that it can still halt before the conflict (about 15 mph).
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, Case C yield control (approach speed reduction)

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
param_proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

param_proposals.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle'. 'The driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'U-turn' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-077 ('the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'), which the concept drv.motion.u_turn carries with that definition: the heading change over the recognition window within the reversal band, integrated across forward and backing moves.

An area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone is the stretch a dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing ('a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}') posts: the travel regions it governs (dev.governs) that x occupies (rel.occupies) of kind st.travel_region. The definitions (DEF-NRS-484B-063 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property', DEF-NRS-484B-060 'those sections of streets ... that pupils cross') describe legal region classes; the ontology reads the sign where the category is also marked on the road. Not a stand-in for whether the posted condition holds now, which prim.conditions_hold reads in exception (e).

Children present are road users of class ru.child ('pedestrian who is visibly a child') whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') that the zone's governed region lies on (st.on_way). Not a stand-in for the roadway: the whole way, sidewalks included, is where children are present in the zone.

A zone designated by a speed limit beacon is one where a dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect') governs (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). 'operational' is read as the beacon not being dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

The yellow lights not flashing in the manner indicating the limit is in effect is the beacon's flashing attribute false: dev.speed_limit_beacon, 'flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect; flashing attribute'.
The zone is not designated by an operational beacon: no dev.speed_limit_beacon that is not dev.inoperative governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies (rel.occupies).

The sign designating the zone is the dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing governing (dev.governs) the region x occupies; its 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend — a list of time windows ...' states when its speed limit is in effect, and the limit is not in effect where prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user') is false.

The section's definition of a speed limit beacon ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately') is what dev.speed_limit_beacon denotes: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'.

assumptions.meaning: The school the zone serves is not in session on the day of the observation.
The observation falls in the period that begins a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and ends a half hour before it next begins operation.
The pupils of the school the zone serves are in class at the observation.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that makes a U-turn: drv.motion.u_turn(x) rises at the judged observation (window p.turn_recognition_window, angles p.reversal_min_angle and p.reversal_max_angle); at some observation while the U-turn is under way (in the window behind the recognition, where drv.motion.turning(x) with p.yaw_rate_tolerance) x occupies a travel region r governed by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing.
obligation: The U-turn is violated unless at every observation while it is under way (throughout) one of the exceptions holds, the same one at each: (a) no ru.child occupies the highway h that r lies on (st.on_way(r, h)); (b) asm.school_not_in_session; (c) asm.school_out_of_operation_period; (d) a dev.speed_limit_beacon b, not dev.inoperative, governs a travel region x occupies, and asm.pupils_in_class, and b's flashing attribute is false; (e) no such operational beacon governs a travel region x occupies, and prim.conditions_hold(z, x) is false. narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever is at the controls.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and: The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle'; 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The intersection is the region the intention is declared at and the vehicle enters: a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'), anchored by the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters).

The right turn lane is a st.turn_lane of side right ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}'). The approach for the turn is the carrier through which x approaches the intersection, which st.lane_enters defines as 'a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'; the turn is made from it when x enters the intersection (rel.occupies of st.intersection rising) out of it. Both are read at the observation before the entry: every carrier x occupies there that enters the intersection is the right turn lane.

The highway has a right turn lane 'as set forth in subsection 4', whose words are 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning': a st.turn_lane of side right ('a lane designated only for turning') that is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane', so ordinal equal to count), lying on (st.on_way) the highway (st.highway) of the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) and entering the intersection x enters (st.lane_enters, st.intersection). The mapping index maps the borrowed words to rel.occupies, st.highway, st.lane_adjacency, st.on_way, st.turn_lane; st.lane_enters and st.intersection tie the lane to this junction.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.
The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the qualifiers 'single', 'right lane' and 'to be used only for turning', which set forth what the highway's right turn lane is; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (driving in that lane only to turn right) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the same qualifiers from the same opening words of subsection 4; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (not travelling through an intersection from that lane) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that enters an intersection i at the judged observation (rel.occupies(x, i) rises), with int.turn_right(x, i) declared true at that observation; and the highway has a right turn lane: at the observation before the entry x occupies a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i), and some st.turn_lane t of side right with st.lane_enters(t, i), lying on the same highway h as c (st.on_way(t, h), st.on_way(c, h)), is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency ordinal equal to count) and is c or a lane reached from c through right-neighbour links of st.lane_adjacency.
obligation: At the observation before the entry, x occupies such a right turn lane t, and every carrier x occupies there that enters i is a st.turn_lane of side right: the approach for the turn and the turn are made from the right turn lane. Violated where x enters i with its intention to turn right from a carrier entering i that is not the right turn lane.

narrowings.why: The approach for the right turn is read at the observation before the entry, as the carrier through which x approaches the intersection then; how far upstream the approach in the turn lane began is not judged.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

scenarios.name: forbid

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car enters the intersection from the right turn lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car with int.turn_left declared and no right-turn intention enters the intersection from the through lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car with int.turn_right enters the intersection; the source does not record which intersection the lanes enter.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car with int.turn_right enters an intersection whose approach has no right turn lane (that case is the extreme-right-lane node's).

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.highway, as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'.
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part is the st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') on the highway (st.on_way), which x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): 'such stopped vehicles' are the vehicles halted upon that part.

Such stopped vehicles are x halted (drv.motion.stopped) upon the roadway. A clear view of them from a distance is st.sight_distance at x's place: 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there'. Not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw x (rel.visible): the words require the view to be available, not that anyone looked. The figure is the law's literal.
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway at the observation.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false; x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: st.sight_distance at x's place is at least the literal 200 ft. Violated where x stands upon the roadway at a place whose sight distance is shorter.

narrowings.why: 'in each direction' is read through the sight distance the source records for the place, which covers the view of approaching traffic and the place's being seen by drivers approaching it; a source that records one figure for the place records the governing (smaller) one.

x's place is read as each roadway x occupies on the highway it occupies (the e1/e6 selection repeated): the sight distance the source records for that roadway region must be at least 200 ft, for every such roadway.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway, district assumption false and disabled assumptions false, a car halts in its lane just beyond a crest where the recorded sight distance is 40 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in its lane on a straight, level stretch whose recorded sight distance is 300 m.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car drives over the crest without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in its lane; the source does not record sight distances.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'.
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', lying on the highway (st.on_way), which x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): the standing vehicle the width is left opposite is one upon that part.

A standing vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not') is x halted, drv.motion.stopped. An unobstructed width of the highway opposite it is a st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') of the same highway (st.on_way) that x's footprint does not overlap (rel.occupies) and that no other halted road user occupies alongside x (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share', not negative).
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway at the observation.

operationalizations.standard: free passage of other vehicles
operationalizations.convention: Free passage of other vehicles is read through the width of the lane left opposite the standing vehicle: st.lane_width ('width of a lane at a point') at least the width a design vehicle needs to pass, so the measured width enters the bound.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false; x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: Some st.lane l with st.on_way(l, h) is not occupied by x, has st.lane_width at least p.free_passage_width, and is occupied alongside x (rel.longitudinal_overlap with x not negative) by no other road user that is halted (drv.motion.stopped). Violated where no such lane is left opposite the standing vehicle.

narrowings.why: The unobstructed width is read as a whole lane of the same highway left beside the standing vehicle, free of other halted road users alongside it; width left in part of a lane, and obstruction by objects other than road users, are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway with two lanes, district assumption false and disabled assumptions false, a car halts in one lane while a truck halts alongside it in the other lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in one lane; the other lane, wider than the free passage width, is free alongside it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car drives along the highway without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in one lane of a two-lane highway; the source supplies no lane widths.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in one lane of a two-lane highway and no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts on a highway whose roadway has a single lane, so no lane is left opposite it.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.free_passage_width
param_proposals.convention: Width a passing design vehicle needs: the 8.5 ft (2.6 m) design vehicle width plus a shy margin of about 0.4 m.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (design vehicle dimensions).

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park
a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within an intersection.

elements.justification: Stop, when prohibited, is DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'); stand is DEF-NRS-484A-250 ('the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of ... receiving or discharging passengers'); park is DEF-NRS-484A-155 ('the standing of a vehicle ... otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of ... loading or unloading'). Each is a halt: drv.motion.stopped (kin.speed at or below its resolution). The stopping definition's exclusions (conflict, officer, device) are the section's own exceptions, which spans c3 to c6 carry. 'A person' is read through the vehicle's conduct.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), the subject's class.

Other traffic is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'), other than x. A halt is necessary to avoid conflict with it where a member is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over the conflict horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance), as the mapping index maps '(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;', or where a member stands ahead of x (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', its longitudinal component positive) within the queue standstill gap of x's body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies'), so that x cannot proceed without striking it.

The directions of a police officer are a dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}') with indication stop, governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies), as the mapping index maps '(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;' to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, st.travel_region.

An official traffic-control device (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating ... traffic') directing a halt is a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign, governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies); its official status is presumed from its presence.

Within an intersection: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'), as the mapping index maps 'within an intersection'. Not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, which lie outside it.

assumptions.meaning: The road user is required to be halted where it is at the observation by a legal duty other than the direction of an officer or a traffic-control device.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies(x, i), st.intersection) at the judged observation.
obligation: Violated where x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) and none of the exceptions holds: (c3) some member z of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than x is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance) or stands ahead of x (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) with rel.surface_gap below p.queue_standstill_gap; (c4) asm.halt_required_by_law; (c5) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region x occupies or i; (c6) a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign governs a travel region x occupies or i.

narrowings.why: 'A person' is read through the vehicle's conduct: a vehicle halted in the intersection is judged whoever or whatever controls it.
The purposes that tell standing and parking from stopping (receiving passengers, loading) are not observable; every halt is read, as each of the three words forbids a halt.
