scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the intersection without halting.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at the curb well away from any intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is within an intersection; the source supplies no speed, so whether it halts is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car waiting to turn left halts within the intersection while an oncoming car is in predicted conflict with it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts within the intersection at a police officer's stop indication governing the intersection; asm.halt_required_by_law declared false.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
param_proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint begins to overlap the intersection: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' on st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the defined word's whole extent (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'); not a crosswalk or stop line, which are other regions.

dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered', which is the words 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered'. 'Controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection': the head governs the intersection or a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; carriers quantified as st.travel_region). Not a position: governance, not where the halt is.
dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' is 'inoperative'; read at the entry observation, the moment the words fix ('at the time the vehicle enters').

The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (ontology section 9); the class is the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. ru.aggregate's exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives' does not apply: the atom is claimed for the vehicle, not for the driver role.

Proceeding as at a stop sign at the entrance the subject uses is the halt the words go on to place: 'stop' when required is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.stopped), made while x occupies (rel.occupies) its approach carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters). The place, in order: st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device' recorded as marking the carrier (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); else st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' marking it, the halt made before the footprint overlaps it; else the carrier's entrance end at st.intersection, with the footprint outside it. At the place is within the stop-point tolerance of it (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), on its upstream side read along the carrier's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along 'the signed distance ... measured along a carrier's designated direction'). Not the distance to a signal head (dev.position).

operationalizations.standard: has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway
operationalizations.convention: The view of approaching traffic on the through highway is a sight distance along that way, st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye', at least the stopping sight distance of the approach-speed design convention (AASHTO stopping sight distance). The through highway is a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') that the intersection lies on (st.on_way 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') and the subject's approach carrier does not.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is judged at each entry of x into an intersection i: an observation at which x's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and at the observation before did not. It applies where, at that entry observation, at least one traffic signal head d (dev.traffic_signal, installed and uncovered) controls i - d governs i itself, or governs a carrier c whose entrance end is i (dev.governs, st.lane_enters) - and every such head that governs i or x's approach carrier is inoperative (dev.inoperative) at that observation.
obligation: Event: the entry of x into i defined in the applicability. Approach: the carrier c (st.travel_region) x occupies at the observation before the entry whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters c i); where x occupies several such carriers and the verdict differs between them, unknown. Place, in the words' order: (1) a stop line s recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c); (2) where the stop-line association of c is observed and lists none, a crosswalk w recorded as marking c, the halt made before x's footprint overlaps w; (3) where neither is recorded for c (associations observed), the entrance end of c at i: a halt with x's footprint outside i, within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, at an observation at which the sight along a through highway h (a st.highway that i lies on and c does not, st.on_way) is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance (st.sight_along_way from x to h). Act: drv.motion.stopped(x) with param p.motion_speed_tolerance at an observation at which x is on c, outside i, on the upstream side of the place (prim.region_offset_along along c's designated direction not past it, a halt on the line counting) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance between x's body and the place); for a crosswalk, also with x's footprint not overlapping it. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start - the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) - or at x's previous entry into i through the same place, whichever is later. A crossing of the mark, a change of carrier within the same entry, a lateral move or speed noise begins no new approach. The duty is met where the search finds the act, violated where it reaches either end without the act, and unknown only where it reaches neither (the recording begins inside the stopping zone with no act recorded). Whether the entry occurred is unknown where the observation before does not place x on a mapped carrier with an observed association to the place; where c's association with a stop line or crosswalk, c's direction or a needed sight distance is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown, never decided from a distance alone.

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'Clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; paint clarity is not modelled.

'The point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view' is read as the entrance end of the approach carrier (outside the intersection, within the stop-point tolerance) at which the view bound is met; a halt farther upstream does not count. 'Proceed as if a stop sign had been erected' is read through the halt the words go on to place; the yield a stop sign also entails is the sibling node's duty.
The driver's view is read as what could be seen from the place along the through highway (st.sight_along_way), not as what the driver perceived.

With every entrance treated as stop-controlled, the through highway is read as any way the intersection lies on that the subject's approach carrier does not lie on; its legal designation is read from the scene.
The search's end at x's previous entry into the intersection is read as any earlier observation at which x occupies the intersection, whichever place that visit came through.
Where several stop lines (or several crosswalks) are recorded as marking the approach carrier, a halt at any one of them meets the duty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.traffic_signal head, uncovered, governs intersection i and is dev.inoperative. x (a passenger car) occupies lane c with st.lane_enters c i; stop line s has st.entrance_of s c. x approaches from 60 m upstream at 10 m/s, slows to 3 m/s near s and enters i without kin.speed ever falling to the speed tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; x halts (kin.speed 0) with its front 0.5 m short of s, on c, then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal head governing i is operating (state circular_green, not dev.inoperative) when x enters i without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe dev.inoperative, so whether the signal was inoperative at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line is recorded for c (association observed, empty); crosswalk w has st.entrance_of w c. x halts with its footprint overlapping w and then enters i.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a stop line nor a crosswalk marks c (associations observed). x halts outside i, 1 m from its edge, where st.sight_along_way to the crossing highway is 120 m, then enters.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with x already on c within the stopping zone of s, rolling at 1 m/s; no halt is recorded before x enters the inoperative-signal intersection, and no approach start is visible.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start of x on c (its last observation outside the stopping zone of s), before the recording begins

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
param_proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

param_proposals.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'. Not a stand-in for the roadway, which e6 reads.

Stop, when prohibited, is DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; park (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of ... loading or unloading') and standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of ... receiving or discharging passengers') are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.stopped (kin.speed at or below its resolution). The stopping definition's exclusion, which the concept's contract does not make, is carried by the rule beside it: a halt necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic (another road user ahead of x in its lane, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, within the queue standstill gap by rel.surface_gap; or one in a predicted conflict with x, prim.closest_approach_within with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance), or one in compliance with an officer's direction (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop) or a device (a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct (agency reading).
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', lying on that highway (st.on_way); x's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). Not a stand-in for the sidewalk: the shoulder and verge are off the roadway, which is where the words direct the vehicle.
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') at the observation.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Practicability of halting off the roadway is read through the space off the roadway beside the vehicle: a st.shoulder lying on the same highway (st.on_way) whose boundary lies within one standard lane width of the vehicle's body (st.region_geometry ground distance from the body outline, compared with the reach), so the distance measured enters the bound, and on which no other halted road user occupies (rel.occupies) the stretch alongside the vehicle (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative). A shoulder farther than the reach, or one taken alongside, makes halting off the roadway not practicable.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither, so no observation of occupancy is read.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h (rel.occupies, st.highway) and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false at the observation; and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: Violated at an observation where x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance), the halt is not excepted, and halting off the roadway is practicable. Excepted halts: some road user z other than x is ahead of x in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap below p.queue_standstill_gap, or is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance); or a device governing a travel region x occupies directs the halt (dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red; dev.stop_sign; dev.yield_sign; dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop). Practicable: some st.shoulder s with st.on_way(s, h) lies within p.off_roadway_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), and no other halted road user occupying s has rel.longitudinal_overlap with x that is not negative.

narrowings.why: 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct: a vehicle halted on the road is judged whoever or whatever controls it.

The purposes that tell parking and standing from stopping (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable; every halt is read, and the halts the stopping definition excepts (to avoid conflict, or in compliance with an officer or a device) are not read as stopping, parking or leaving the vehicle standing.

Practicability is read only through a shoulder of the same highway beside the vehicle and free alongside it; other places off the roadway (a turnout, a verge without a mapped shoulder) and the shoulder's surface and width are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway, asm.business_or_residence_district declared false and both disabled assumptions declared false, a car halts in the right lane for a minute; a free shoulder lies beside it within the reach; no other road user and no device is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same halt on a highway with no shoulder within the reach of the car's body.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same halt with asm.business_or_residence_district declared true.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with no speed observed, so whether the car is halted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane behind a stopped truck within the queue standstill gap, with a free shoulder beside it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane with asm.vehicle_disabled and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable declared true.

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
param_proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.off_roadway_reach
param_proposals.convention: One standard lane width (12 ft): a shoulder separated from the vehicle's body by no more than one lane is reachable by one lateral move, and is beside the vehicle.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (standard 12 ft travel lane).

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character at:
A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: drv.motion.moving, 'a road user is in motion at the observation ... whoever or whatever controls the road user'; a vehicle at rest has no rate of speed the standard could find unreasonable. 'any person' names who controls the vehicle, a role read through the vehicle's conduct (observable_reading, agency).

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), one atom, never expanded; 'of any kind or character' adds no class beyond the definition's.

operationalizations.standard: A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-sight-distance model (AASHTO Green Book): a speed is reasonable only where the vehicle can halt, after a perception-reaction time and at the deceleration the surface sustains, within the distance it can see along the road (st.sight_distance) and through the air (env.visibility); the surface selects that deceleration (ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry). Traffic: time-headway convention, the speed times the minimum time headway within the gap to each road user of the traffic ahead in the lane. Other highway conditions: the lateral acceleration in a bend (speed squared times st.curvature) within the acceleration the surface sustains. Width: time-to-line-crossing convention, the speed times the lateral margin needed per unit of speed within the free lateral margin, half of the lane width less the vehicle width. Each measured magnitude enters its bound, so the bound moves with the speed, the gap, the distances, the curvature and the width; the surface condition selects among bounds.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is being driven: x is in motion (drv.motion.moving, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance).
obligation: Surrogate. At the observation x's speed (kin.speed) meets every bound the factors set. Let a be the surface's deceleration: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_dry; the stopping distance SD is drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), written as a Term.cond over the three calls, each with its own constant parameter. (1) SD is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) and at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (2) For every road user y other than x that is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), x's speed times p.following_min_time_headway is at most the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap). (3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x's speed times p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed is at most half of the difference between the lane's width (st.lane_width) and x's width (kin.extent, width). Violated where any bound fails.

narrowings.why: 'any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel') is read only through the road users ahead of x in its own lane, every one of which is using the way for travel, by the time headway to each; oncoming, crossing and adjacent-lane traffic, and traffic on a way with no mapped lane, set no bound.
'surface' is read through env.wet_road and env.ice_or_snow, which select the deceleration; surface texture, loose material and damage carry no atom and are not read.

'width of the highway' is read through the width of the lane x occupies (st.lane_width), the strip its travel uses, not the whole width between the highway's boundary lines; where x occupies no mapped lane the width sets no bound.
'the weather' is read through env.visibility, by its degree, and env.precipitation, which selects the wet deceleration; wind and temperature are not read.
The catch-all 'other highway conditions' is read only through st.sight_distance and st.curvature; grade, works and other conditions are not read.

'the sight distance at x's place' and 'the curvature at x's place' are read on each lane x occupies (st.lane, rel.occupies), the regions the width bound reads; where x occupies no mapped lane, sight distance and curvature set no bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x, alone in the scene, drives on a dry road in dense fog at a speed whose stopping distance far exceeds the visibility distance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x, alone in the scene, drives at a moderate speed on a dry, straight road with wide lanes in clear weather and a long sight distance; its stopping distance lies within the sight and visibility distances and the lane-keeping margin holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x stands halted throughout the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.speed absent: whether x moves, and how fast, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Clear, dry, straight road; x follows y, a car in the same lane, at a gap shorter than its speed times the minimum time headway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x drives through a bend on an icy road at a speed whose lateral acceleration exceeds the ice deceleration, though it would lie within the dry one.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The same bend and speed as branch_2 on a dry road in clear weather, every other bound met.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A wide vehicle x travels in a narrow lane at a speed whose required lateral margin exceeds half of the lane width less its width; every other bound is met.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_wet
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration a wet paved surface sustains: a wet-pavement friction coefficient of about a quarter at highway speeds, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: Pavement skid-resistance data (AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction)

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration an icy or snow-covered surface sustains: a friction coefficient of about a tenth, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: Winter road friction measurements (PIARC Snow and Ice Databook)

param_proposals.name: p.following_min_time_headway
param_proposals.convention: Car-following: the smallest time gap to the road user ahead at which a following driver can still react to its braking; gaps below it are classed as close following.
param_proposals.source: Time-headway criteria of naturalistic driving and traffic-flow studies

param_proposals.name: p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-line-crossing convention: drifting at a heading error of about one degree, a vehicle keeps at least one second before its body reaches the lane edge, so the free lateral margin it needs is its speed times the sine of that error times that time.
param_proposals.source: Godthelp, Milgram and Blaauw (1984), time-to-line-crossing

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle,
moped or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and (4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'several states may be displayed at once': circular_red with green_arrow(left) or green_arrow(right), governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection); read at the entry.
'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle; 'A person driving' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'moped' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition; nearest class atom ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants'; a three-wheeler driven from a seat is not denoted, so a gap is recorded.
The admitted aggregates for bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter, each claimed as its aggregate.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the carrier occupied at the observation before entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, dev.governs, rel.occupies), or the intersection itself.

The permitted movements: drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i), or the turn opposite the arrow, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(left) and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(right), recognized at the exit from the heading change since entry (kin.yaw_rate) over the overlap with the intersection.

Another device prohibiting the turn is a dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... no_left_turn, no_right_turn ...', with the code for the turn made (no_left_turn for a left turn, no_right_turn for a right turn), at the place: governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier x occupied before entry (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection); a sign with conditions prohibits where prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user'). Not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: the sign is the condition, the turn is read by the movement concept.

'if applicable' limits the requirement to a movement that is a turn: the crossing is drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) or drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i); a through movement makes no turn a device could prohibit.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle; at the judged observation x leaves intersection i; at its entry (read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing x's approach carrier c (dev.governs(s, c), st.lane_enters(c, i)) or i displayed circular_red with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing is a turn opposite the arrow (if applicable): drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is right.
obligation: At the entry (read through a past operator from the exit): no dev.regulatory_sign g of code no_right_turn (for a right turn) or no_left_turn (for a left turn) governs c or i (dev.governs(g, c) or dev.governs(g, i)) with prim.conditions_hold(g, x). Violated where such a sign governs the approach or the intersection with its conditions holding.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

A device prohibiting the turn is read as a regulatory sign of the turn's code governing the approach or the intersection, its official status presumed from its presence; a prohibition expressed only by a lane marking arrow is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle on an approach governed by a signal showing circular_red with green_arrow(left) and by a no_right_turn sign with empty conditions enters and turns right.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same right turn at an approach with no regulatory sign of a turn code.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The motorcycle goes straight through on red with a green left arrow: no turn is made, so the requirement is not applicable.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle turns right on red with a green left arrow; the source does not observe regulatory signs.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
param_proposals.convention: The heading change to the left beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift.
param_proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

param_proposals.name: p.reversal_min_angle

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,
to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping
due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;
or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own.

st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before.

'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry).

'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x.

The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3).

assumptions.meaning: The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.
obligation: Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.

'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.

The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver,
having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: The left-turning party y is a vehicle: DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported').
y's footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', st.intersection); the region y's intention is declared at.

A signal of a left turn is sig.turn_indicator state left ('the left or the right one') or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'); 'not a stand-in for the turn itself' respected - the signal is read as the signal. 'When and as required' points to signalling rules outside this corpus; carried as the words say: a left signal shown by y at some observation since it last came onto its approach carrier, continuing into the turn.
The other drivers are drivers of vehicles: the vehicle aggregate, the subject x, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

x approaches i through a carrier cx it occupies with st.lane_enters cx i ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into'); 'from the opposite direction' is read, per rel.oncoming's contract, through the carriers' designated directions: st.lane_direction of cx and of y's approach carrier cy have a dot product below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance.
Yielding is not moving into the intersection (drv.motion.moving with rel.occupies of st.intersection) while the turning vehicle's precedence is owed.
The vehicle making the left turn: y's heading is turning to the left (drv.motion.turning_left) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a left turn at the target region.

residues.why: The permission to make the turn adds nothing to the condition: the vehicle yielded to is the one 'making the left turn' (s13), which already requires the turn under way.

applicability: x is a vehicle occupying a carrier cx with st.lane_enters cx i (approaching intersection i; its entry observation, overlapping both, included), and there is a vehicle y other than x such that: y's footprint overlaps i; the declaration current at the observation states y intends to turn left at i (int.turn_left y i); y's approach carrier cy (the carrier with st.lane_enters cy i it occupied when its current occupancy of i began) has a designated direction opposed to cx's (dot product of st.lane_direction below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance); y has complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (x of that rule mapped to y) at every observation since its current occupancy of i began; y showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since it last came onto cy; and y is turning left within i (drv.motion.turning_left with p.yaw_rate_tolerance).
obligation: At an observation at which x's footprint overlaps i and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), there is no vehicle y meeting every condition of the applicability (bound again with the whole selection) whose centres and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The drivers are read through the vehicles' controlled motion.
Yielding is judged where x moves into or within the intersection; slowing on the approach is not separately checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: y occupies i with int.turn_left y i, entered from cy heading north, showed sig.turn_indicator left on cy, yielded to oncoming traffic (no conflict while it moved), and is now turning left (yaw rate 15 deg/s). x approaches on cx heading south and moves into i; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x halts on cx short of i until y has cleared, then enters.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x approaches i on cx; no vehicle within i is turning left.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but neither the turn indicator nor arm signals are observed, so whether y gave a signal is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but y showed no signal (sig.turn_indicator off and sig.hand_signal no_signal throughout its approach).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but y moved into its turn earlier while an oncoming vehicle within i was in predicted conflict, so y has not complied with NRS_484B_253_o1.

param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance

param_proposals.source: Intersection leg geometry convention (AASHTO Green Book: legs intersecting at angles near 90 degrees)

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle,
moped or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and (4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'several states may be displayed at once': circular_red with green_arrow(left) or green_arrow(right), governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection); read at the entry.
'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle; 'A person driving' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'moped' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition; nearest class atom ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants'; a three-wheeler driven from a seat is not denoted, so a gap is recorded.
The admitted aggregates for bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter, each claimed as its aggregate.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the carrier occupied at the observation before entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, dev.governs, rel.occupies), or the intersection itself.

The permitted movements: drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i), or the turn opposite the arrow, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(left) and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(right), recognized at the exit from the heading change since entry (kin.yaw_rate) over the overlap with the intersection.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: the other's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another ... approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash') is read as x, while moving (drv.motion.moving) in the intersection, never standing in a predicted conflict with the parties: prim.closest_approach_within over the conflict horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance, the primitives that state direction, speed and proximity under constant velocities. The pedestrians are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...') whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an adjacent crosswalk: a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters), a crossing of the junction itself. Other traffic is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway') other than x whose footprint overlaps the intersection (st.intersection, rel.occupies).

applicability: As NRS_484B_307_9b_o1: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle; at the judged observation x leaves intersection i; at its entry (read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing x's approach carrier c (dev.governs(s, c), st.lane_enters(c, i)) or i displayed circular_red with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing is a through movement or a turn opposite the arrow (drv.motion.straight_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region under a left arrow, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region under a right arrow).
obligation: At every observation from x's entry into i to its exit (read with since from the exit), wherever x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance): for every pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk w with st.entrance_of(w, c2) and st.lane_enters(c2, i) for some carrier c2, and for every member z of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than x occupying i, not both prim.closest_approach_within(x, ·) over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(x, ·) over that horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Violated where x moves in a predicted conflict with such a party during the crossing; with no such party present the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'lawfully within' and 'lawfully using' are read as within and using: the lawfulness of the pedestrian's or the other road user's own conduct is the verdict of rules this corpus does not state, so every pedestrian in an adjacent crosswalk and every other member of traffic in the intersection is yielded to. The yield is judged over the crossing of the intersection, from the entry to the exit.

scenarios.narrative: The bicycle waits in the intersection until the pedestrian has cleared, so no predicted conflict arises while it moves.

scenarios.narrative: The bicycle enters on red with a green left arrow and turns left with the arrow.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle goes straight through on red with a green left arrow while a pedestrian on a crosswalk at the intersection is in predicted conflict with it; the source does not record which approach the crosswalk marks.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle goes straight through on red with a green left arrow and no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A moped turns right on red with a green left arrow while a car turning left with the arrow, already in the intersection, is in predicted conflict with it as it moves.

A person driving a motorcycle,
moped or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change

(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left) or green_arrow(right); circular_red is the steady red, flashing_red being a separate state. The signal is the one governing the road user's approach (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'): the carrier of kind st.travel_region the road user occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), or the intersection (st.intersection) itself. Not a stand-in for a position: governance says which device applies, not where to halt. The display is read at the entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to ('facing the signal may proceed').

'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels ...'); claimed as the aggregate. 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

'moped' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition and no aggregate; the nearest class atom is ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants', which denotes the three-wheeled machines ridden astride; a three-wheeled motor vehicle driven from a seat is not ridden astride and is not denoted, so a gap is recorded for it.

The admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ...') and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor'); each claimed as its aggregate. 'riding' is read through the device's controlled motion.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the approach the road user enters through, the carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), dev.governs naming the carrier, or governing the intersection itself. The road user's heading is not read: st.lane_enters states that the approach is the carrier occupied, 'never ... the road user's velocity or heading'.

Proceeding straight through is drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i) at x's exit from the intersection; turning in the direction opposite the arrow is drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where the green arrow displayed at entry is green_arrow(left), and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where it is green_arrow(right); each concept reads the heading change since entry integrated from kin.yaw_rate over the overlap with the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection). The permission's movement is recognized where the crossing ends, the exit.

'stops' is a required stop, DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('complete cessation from movement'), the concept drv.motion.stopped ('the definition's "complete cessation from movement"'). The place is read on the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters): the pavement marking that indicates where the stop must be made is a st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', recorded as marking that carrier's entrance (st.entrance_of, 'exactly that carrier's entrance'); failing one, the crosswalk on the nearest side, a st.crosswalk the source records as marking that carrier's entrance; failing both, the entrance end of the carrier at the intersection (st.intersection). Whether the halt lies short of the place is read along the carrier's designated direction by prim.region_offset_along and the body-to-mark distance by st.region_geometry, as the ontology's approach convention states. Not a stand-in for distance to the line: the line's association is the source's record.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle (the trimobile); at the judged observation x leaves an intersection i; at x's entry into i (the observation at which x's overlap with i last became true, read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c that x occupied at the observation before the entry (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing x completes is a through movement (drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i)) or a turn opposite the arrow (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is right), with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and the angles p.straight_through_max_heading_change, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.right_turn_min_angle, p.reversal_min_angle.
obligation: Trigger: the entry of x into i found by the applicability. Place: on the approach carrier c, the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of) where one is recorded; else the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance, on the near side; else c's entrance end at i. Act: x halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) while on c at the place: within p.stop_point_tolerance of the mark by body distance (st.region_geometry), not beyond it along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along), and with its footprint not overlapping the crosswalk (for the crosswalk place) or i (for the intersection place). History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the mark is recorded as marking, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it and farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from it), or at x's previous entry into i, whichever is later; nothing else ends it. A halt found: met. Either end reached without a halt: violated. Neither end reached without a halt (the approach began before the recording): unknown. A mark whose entrances are observed and exclude c does not govern, and the next place in the words' order is read; a mark whose association with c is unobserved leaves the place unknown where the verdict depends on it.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' names who controls the motorcycle, moped or trimobile; read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The sign or pavement marking that 'indicates where the stop must be made' is read through the stop line the source records as marking the approach's entrance; a sign that indicates a stopping place without a line is not read as a place of its own.

Where x occupied several approach carriers into the intersection at the observation before its entry, the halt is required at the place of each carrier, rather than leaving the verdict unknown where the carriers' places give different verdicts.

The approach start that ends the search for a halt is read on the approach carrier itself (the carrier the mark is recorded as marking for this approach), not on another carrier the same mark is recorded as marking.

segmentation.text: An operator of a bicycle,
an electric bicycle
or an electric scooter
upon a roadway
shall give all signals by hand and arm
in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],
except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.

elements.justification: 'bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride ... except a moped'), one atom. 'An operator of' is the rider, a role read through the machine's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'electric bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), one atom, never expanded.

'electric scooter' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on in an upright or seated position'), one atom, never expanded. Which road-user classes it includes is the run's reading, not this record's: where the reading leaves a class unresolved under it, ru.aggregate is unknown for a road user of that class, and the rule reports unknown for it, never compliance or violation.

DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its 'not a stand-in for the sidewalk' clause is the definition's own exclusion. 'upon' anchors it to x by rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; a one-way roadway refines st.roadway and is included.

'give all signals by hand and arm': sig.hand_signal is 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', the signal given by hand and arm; sig.turn_indicator is 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', the signal given otherwise. Every turn signal the rider gives by lamp is to be a signal by hand and arm of the same meaning. The manner borrowed from DEF-NRS-484B-420 ('extended horizontally') is the posture whose meaning the source reads into sig.hand_signal. sig.turn_indicator's 'not a stand-in for the turn itself' is respected: the lamp is read as a signal, never as the turn.

The exception permits a second posture for one meaning: a right-turn signal given 'by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side'. sig.hand_signal carries the meaning of the arm signal given, right, whichever arm and posture give it, so the right-arm signal and the posture the borrowed manner states both read as meaning right and both meet the duty.

applicability: x is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at the observation.
obligation: At the observation, every turn signal x gives is given by hand and arm: where x's turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator) shows left, x's arm signal (sig.hand_signal) has meaning left, and where it shows right, x's arm signal has meaning right. An arm signal of meaning right meets the duty whichever arm gives it (the exception). An arm signal given with no lamp, and no signal at all, are compliant: this rule judges how signals are given, not whether one is owed.

narrowings.why: 'An operator of' is read through the controlled motion of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, whoever or whatever controls it.

'all signals' is read as the turn signals the rider gives by lamp (sig.turn_indicator): a brake lamp lights as an actuation of the brake, which its contract separates from a signal the rider gives, so it is not read; the posture of the arm beyond the meaning the source reads from it is not read.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions classified by the reading); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: the entry (x's footprint begins to overlap the controlled-access region, rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region ... controlled-access lane') or the exit (it ceases to overlap it, onto another st.highway region).

Yielding is not making the entry or exit (the change of x's overlap with the controlled-access region, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) into a predicted conflict with a vehicle owed precedence.

All vehicles y (aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) approaching on the highway: y moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint on the highway being entered - the controlled-access region at an entry, the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: a vehicle on the highway is an immediate hazard where the gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is at most its speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap, so the bound moves with its speed.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into a controlled-access region a (st.controlled_access): an observation at which x's footprint overlaps a and did not at the observation before; and at each exit: an observation at which x's footprint no longer overlaps a and did at the observation before; where there is a vehicle y other than x on the highway being entered - at an entry, y's footprint overlaps a; at an exit, y's footprint overlaps a st.highway region that x's footprint overlaps at that observation, and not a - that is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) and whose body gap to x (rel.surface_gap) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving at the judged observation (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'About to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: the observation of entry into, or exit from, the controlled-access region.
The yield is judged at the observation of entry or exit; 'the highway' is read as the highway being entered: the controlled-access highway at an entry, the highway x moves onto at an exit.

scenarios.name: blind
