scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x leaves a onto a crossroad (st.highway) and moves across it while y on the crossroad, 10 m away at 13 m/s, is in predicted conflict (1 m in 0.9 s).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_time_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap of gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle whose time to reach the conflict (its distance over its speed) is at most this gap is an immediate hazard to a turning, crossing or merging manoeuvre.
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual, base critical headway (4.1 s for a major-street left turn)

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle,
moped or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and (4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left) or green_arrow(right). It is the signal governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier of kind st.travel_region the road user occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection) itself; read at the entry, the event the words fix it to.
'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle ...'); 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'moped' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition; nearest class atom ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants'; a three-wheeler driven from a seat is not denoted, so a gap is recorded.
The admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, each claimed as its aggregate.

Facing the signal: the signal governs (dev.governs) the carrier the road user occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection itself; the heading is not read, as st.lane_enters states.

Proceeding straight through is drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i); the turn opposite the arrow is drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(left) and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) under green_arrow(right); each reads the heading change since entry from kin.yaw_rate and the overlap with the intersection, recognized at the exit.

Waiting is staying on the approach without entering the intersection after the halt (drv.motion.stopped, a required stop of DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') that begins the wait, on the carrier (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters). The applicable official traffic-control device is the dev.traffic_signal governing (dev.governs) that approach or the intersection. A complete cycle of its lighted arrows is one display of the green turn arrow (green_arrow(dir)) that lights and then goes out while the road user waits. 'Two complete cycles' is a number of such cycles, not a magnitude: it is written as two completed cycles, one ending strictly after the other, both within the wait, so the formula states no numeric threshold for it and the record declares no literal. The signal not changing is the governing signal displaying no circular_green at any observation of the wait.

residues.why: The cause the words name (a malfunction, or a failure to detect the road user) is what a signal's not changing for a waiting road user through two complete cycles consists in; once the obligation reads two complete cycles with no change, the cause adds no further restriction, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

applicability: As NRS_484B_307_9b_o1: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle; at the judged observation x leaves an intersection i; at x's entry into i (the observation at which x's overlap with i last became true, read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c that x occupied at the observation before the entry (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing is a through movement (drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i)) or a turn opposite the arrow (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is right), with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and the angles p.straight_through_max_heading_change, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.right_turn_min_angle, p.reversal_min_angle.
obligation: For every intersection i, arrow direction dir, signal s and carrier c selected as in the applicability (the whole selection bound again; every selected signal and carrier is held to the duty, a rule never picking the one that favours the road user), at x's entry into i (read through a past operator from the exit), at the observation before the entry: the wait is the stretch from the latest rise of H = x halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) while occupying c and not i. Through the stretch x did not occupy i and s displayed no circular_green at any observation. A cycle of the arrow ends at a rise of E = green_arrow(dir) of s is out, and has risen at some observation since H's latest rise. Two complete cycles ended within the wait: E rose at some observation since H's latest rise and, at an observation before that rise at which E did not hold, E had already risen since H's latest rise (written with since and rises, no numeric threshold). Met where all of this holds; violated where x entered after fewer than two completed arrow cycles in its wait, or after s had displayed circular_green during it. Where the wait began before the recording (no rise of H observed), the wait and its cycles are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The 'applicable official traffic-control device' is the signal head present and governing the approach; its official status is presumed from its presence.

A complete cycle of the lights or lighted arrows is read as one display of the green turn arrow that lights and goes out within the wait; a cycle of the circular indications without an arrow display is not counted separately.

The stretch of the wait is read up to the observation before the entry, the last at which the road user does not occupy the intersection; the entry observation itself belongs to the crossing, so the signal's indications there are read only by the applicability.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes'; 'about to' read by the movement it leads to: entry into or exit from the controlled-access region (rel.occupies changing), onto another st.highway region at an exit.

The referent of 'that traffic': vehicles y (aggregate) moving (drv.motion.moving) on the highway being entered (rel.occupies of the controlled-access region at an entry, of the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit).
Continuing to yield is not making the entry or exit (x's overlap with the controlled-access region changing, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) before it may proceed safely.

'That traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') refers to the vehicles of s4-s5 whose proximity was an immediate hazard; the rule reads them as traffic members of the vehicle aggregate with every qualification s4-s5 state.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: the body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: may proceed with reasonable safety
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: x may proceed with reasonable safety once no vehicle of that traffic has a predicted closest approach to x within the time-to-collision horizon below the centre clearance.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into a controlled-access region a (x's footprint overlaps a and did not at the observation before) and each exit (it no longer overlaps a and did at the observation before), where there is a vehicle y other than x of that traffic: at some observation of the run of observations immediately before that event during which x stayed on the near side (for an entry, off a; for an exit, on a), y was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on the highway being entered (a at an entry; at an exit, a st.highway region x's footprint overlaps at the exit, not a) with a body gap to x (rel.surface_gap) at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving at the event observation (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of that traffic (bound again with its whole selection) has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'About to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region.
'Reasonable safety' is read only as the absence of a predicted conflict with that traffic at the moment x proceeds; no other factor is read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x waits on the ramp off a while y on a, 20 m away at 25 m/s, is an immediate hazard; x then enters a while y is still in predicted conflict (1.5 m in 1 s).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same hazard while x waits; x enters only after y has passed and no conflict with y is predicted.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no vehicle on a ever within speed times the critical gap during its approach.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies is not observed: whether x entered or exited the controlled-access region, and whether y was on the highway being entered, are unknown, so whether the duty arose is unknown while the predicted conflict is still decided.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no other road user in the scene: no hazard arose, so no continued yield is owed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The exit limb: x travels on a while y, moving on the highway region h beside a, is within its speed times the critical gap of x; x exits a onto h while y is in predicted conflict with it.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter or proceed through an intersection
while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.

elements.justification: Motor vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'; 'does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as the admitted aggregate and never expanded; the driver is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (ontology §9: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct).

Entering or proceeding through an intersection: the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', matching DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join', and excluding an alley junction as the definition's (3) does) — rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') true at this observation and false at the observation before; every passage through an intersection begins with that entry.

Driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters: x in motion (drv.motion.moving: kin.speed above the speed-resolution tolerance, 'whoever or whatever controls the road user') with its footprint overlapping a region of kind st.bicycle_lane_or_path ('lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them') through rel.occupies; the words name the lane's purpose, not road users, so no aggregate is claimed.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) with its footprint on a bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path), and where NRS_484B_270_3_o2 applies to x (its x mapped to x): none of subsection 3's exceptions (a)-(f) excuses x's presence in the lane.
obligation: x does not enter an intersection at the judged observation: it is not the case that, for some intersection i, x's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) here and did not at the observation before.

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'Proceed through' is read at the entry into the intersection, where every passage through it begins.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x drives in bicycle lane b up to intersection i and its footprint enters i while still on b; no exception holds and the trace declares asm.vehicle_disabled, asm.performing_official_duties and asm.emergency false.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x drives in b mid-block (no exception holds) and does not enter an intersection while in it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x enters i from a general traffic lane, never on a bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but kin.speed is not observed, so whether x is driving (in motion) in the bicycle lane when it enters i cannot be read; occupancy stays observed, so subsection 3's rule remains decided.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs b and directs x through it: subsection 3's exception (e) holds, so NRS_484B_270_3_o2 does not apply.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle,
an electric bicycle
or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.

The driver of a motor vehicle shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway; (b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle; (c) To avoid conflict with other traffic; (d) In the performance of official duties; (e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer; or (f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding on the pathway or lane is not moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on the bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) into a predicted conflict with a road user owed precedence there.
A person riding a bicycle: DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), the ridden road user.
DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts').
DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on').
DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'), limited by s8 to a pedestrian in the situation subsection 6 provides for.

On the pathway or lane: the road user yielded to has its footprint on st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them' (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path b (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where there is a road user y other than x whose footprint overlaps b and which is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter), or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) to which NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies (its x mapped to y): a pedestrian on a detour around a sidewalk obstruction, that is, y's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and y has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which y was moving on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h) with an obstruction within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of its body or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable holding.
obligation: No road user y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection: other than x, footprint on b, and a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, or a pedestrian to which NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies with its x mapped to y) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is judged where the motor vehicle moves with its footprint on the pathway or lane; slowing before reaching it is not separately checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (passenger car) turns right across bicycle lane b and moves onto it while a bicycle y rides in b behind it at 6 m/s; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while bicycle y in b is 40 m away at 5 m/s and predicted to pass 15 m from x.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x never occupies a bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies is not observed, so whether x and y are on b is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while a pedestrian who walked into b from a crosswalk (no sidewalk detour, NRS_484B_297_6_o2 not applying) is in predicted conflict: that pedestrian is not one the duty protects.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while a pedestrian y detouring around a sidewalk obstruction walks in b, predicted closest approach about 1 m within 1 s. The scene states every fact NRS_484B_297_6_o2's applicability reads: a highway region h (st.highway) spanning the whole way, travel lane, b and sidewalk w included, with w recorded as lying on h (st.on_way w h) and b lying on h; an obstruction (st.obstruction, kind sidewalk_fixture) on w with its outline (st.region_geometry) observed. y first walks on w at walking speed (moving above p.motion_speed_tolerance) and at one such observation its body touches the obstruction (distance zero, within p.obstruction_encounter_reach); from the next observation on y's footprint overlaps b and h and overlaps no sidewalk at all (its body clear of w's edge), continuously to the end of the trace, walking on in b beside the obstruction toward x. The conflict observations come after the step off the sidewalk, inside the detour.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As branch_2 in every fact but one: no obstruction is anywhere in the scene and asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable is declared false at every observation, so y steps from w into b without a detour and NRS_484B_297_6_o2 does not apply to it; the same predicted conflict leaves the duty unengaged.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'several states may be displayed at once': circular_red displayed with green_arrow(dir), governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection); read at the entry, the event the words fix it to.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ...'); the qualifier 'vehicular' leaves out pedestrians, read by the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian as a condition beside it (x is not a pedestrian), and ridden or herded animals, which no class atom carries.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the approach carrier x occupies at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, dev.governs, rel.occupies), or the intersection itself.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: the other's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another ... approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash') is read as x, while moving (drv.motion.moving) in the intersection, never standing in a predicted conflict with the parties: prim.closest_approach_within over the conflict horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance. Pedestrians are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian occupying (rel.occupies) an adjacent crosswalk, a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters); other traffic is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, other than x, occupying the intersection (st.intersection).

residues.why: An advisory statement of the signal phasing (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no duty of the road user turns on it.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and not of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; at the judged observation x occupies an intersection i and has occupied it at every observation since its entry (the rise of its overlap with i), and at that entry a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c x occupied at the observation before it (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with at least one green_arrow(dir) (read with since: occupancy of i since the entry under that display). The duty does not apply where a node of paragraph (b) applies (NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 to _o4, ruleApplies with x mapped to x).
obligation: Wherever x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance): for every pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk w with st.entrance_of(w, c2) and st.lane_enters(c2, i) for some carrier c2, and every member z of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than x occupying i, not both prim.closest_approach_within(x, ·) over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(x, ·) over that horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. With no such party present the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' and 'lawfully using' are read as within and using: the lawfulness of the other road user's own conduct is the verdict of rules this corpus does not state, so every pedestrian in an adjacent crosswalk and every other member of traffic in the intersection is yielded to. The yield is judged while x crosses the intersection it entered under the arrow.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and turns left while a pedestrian walks in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the cross street's approach; while the car moves their predicted closest approach within the horizon is below the conflict clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts inside the intersection until the pedestrian has cleared and turns with no predicted conflict while it moves.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car enters on circular_green and turns left.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car turns on the arrow while a pedestrian on a crosswalk at the intersection is in predicted conflict with it; the source does not record which approach the crosswalk marks.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters on red with a green left arrow and turns left with no other road user in the scene.
